sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the packaged program
sections.what: Imports the multiprocessing setup helper and the main command function from the app.
sections.why: Gives the packaged program the same behavior as running the app normally.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Packaged startup
sections.what: Sets up multiprocessing support and runs the main command when this file starts the program.
sections.why: Likely reason: multiprocessing needs this setup in a packaged program so child processes start correctly.
sections.watch_out: Removing the setup call can make child processes fail only in the packaged build, not in normal runs.

summary: The starting point used when the app is packaged into a standalone program, which calls the normal command-line entry point.
purpose: Gives the packaging tool a single file to turn into the Windows application.
why: Likely reason: packaging tools need a plain entry file, and this one applies multiprocessing setup before the normal command runs.
how: It imports the standard multiprocessing setup and the main command. When run directly, it sets up multiprocessing support and then starts the main command.
inputs: Command-line arguments passed to the packaged program.
outputs: Whatever the main command does, such as starting the local web server.
risks: If the main command changes name, this file breaks the packaged build.
debug: If the packaged program fails to start, run this file directly from Python first to see whether the import or the command is at fault.
